items.informal_name: Product Rule for Hasse Derivatives in Polynomial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f g : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) (f * g) =
    ∑ ij ∈ Finset.antidiagonal k, (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.1) f * (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.2) g
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $ f, g \in R[X] $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the product $ f \cdot g $ satisfies $$ D^{(k)}(f \cdot g) = \sum_{\substack{i + j = k}} D^{(i)}(f) \cdot D^{(j)}(g), $$ where the sum is taken over all pairs $ (i, j) $ of natural numbers such that $ i + j = k $. This expresses the Hasse derivative of a product as a sum over the antidiagonal decomposition of $ k $.

items.informal_name: Product Rule for Partial Derivatives in Multivariate Polynomial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {σ : Type v} [inst : CommSemiring R] {i : σ} {f g : MvPolynomial σ R},
  (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) (f * g) = (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) f * g + f * (MvPolynomial.pderiv i) g
items.informal_description: For any commutative semiring $ R $, type $ \sigma $, and variables $ i \in \sigma $, the partial derivative with respect to $ i $ of the product of two multivariate polynomials $ f $ and $ g $ in $ R[\sigma] $ satisfies the Leibniz rule: $ \partial_i(fg) = (\partial_i f) \cdot g + f \cdot (\partial_i g) $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k on Polynomial Ring
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → ℕ → Polynomial R →ₗ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ is an $ R $-linear map $ D^{(k)} : R[X] 	o R[X] $ defined by $ D^{(k)}(a_i X^i) =  inom{i}{k} a_i X^{i - k} $ on monomials and extended linearly. This operation generalizes the usual derivative by scaling each coefficient $ a_i $ by the binomial coefficient $  inom{i}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative Composition Formula with Binomial Coefficient
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k l : ℕ),
  Polynomial.hasseDeriv k ∘ₗ Polynomial.hasseDeriv l = (k + l).choose k • Polynomial.hasseDeriv (k + l)
items.informal_description: For any semiring $ R $ and natural numbers $ k, l $, the composition of the $ k $-th and $ l $-th Hasse derivatives on the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ equals $ \binom{k + l}{k} $ times the $ (k + l) $-th Hasse derivative, i.e., $ D^{(k)} \circ D^{(l)} = \binom{k + l}{k} D^{(k + l)} $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Monomial in Polynomial Ring
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k n : ℕ) (r : R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) ((Polynomial.monomial n) r) = (Polynomial.monomial (n - k)) (↑(n.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the monomial $ rX^n $ in the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ is given by $ \binom{n}{k} r X^{n - k} $. This expresses how the Hasse derivative acts on monomials by scaling the coefficient by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{n}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k Applied to a Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f = f.sum fun i r => (Polynomial.monomial (i - k)) (↑(i.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $ and a polynomial $ f \in R[X] $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ applied to $ f $ is given by $ D^{(k)}(f) = \sum_{i} \binom{i}{k} \cdot a_i \cdot X^{i - k} $, where $ a_i $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ f $. This expression sums over all monomials in $ f $, scaling each by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{i}{k} $ and reducing the exponent by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Bind₂ of Monomial: $ \text{bind₂}(f)(r X^d) = f(r) X^d $
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} {S : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S]
  (f : R →+* MvPolynomial σ S) (d : σ →₀ ℕ) (r : R),
  (MvPolynomial.bind₂ f) ((MvPolynomial.monomial d) r) = f r * (MvPolynomial.monomial d) 1
items.informal_description: For any ring homomorphism $ f : R \to R[\sigma] $, finite support function $ d : \sigma \to₀ \mathbb{N} $, and coefficient $ r \in R $, applying the bind₂ operation to the monomial $ r X^d $ yields $ f(r) X^d $, where $ X^d $ denotes the monomial with exponents specified by $ d $ and coefficient 1.

items.informal_name: Additivity of Elementary Symmetric Polynomial Substitution for Monomials
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} {n : ℕ} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : Fintype σ] {r : R} {t s : Fin n →₀ ℕ},
  MvPolynomial.esymmAlgHomMonomial σ (t + s) r =
    MvPolynomial.esymmAlgHomMonomial σ t r * MvPolynomial.esymmAlgHomMonomial σ s 1
items.informal_description: For any finite support functions $ t $ and $ s $ from $ \text{Fin } n $ to $ \mathbb{N} $, the elementary symmetric polynomial substitution for the monomial with exponent $ t + s $ and coefficient $ r $ equals the product of the substitution for the monomial with exponent $ t $ and coefficient $ r $ and the substitution for the monomial with exponent $ s $ and coefficient $ 1 $. Formally, $ \text{esymmAlgHomMonomial}_\sigma(t + s, r) = \text{esymmAlgHomMonomial}_\sigma(t, r) \cdot \text{esymmAlgHomMonomial}_\sigma(s, 1) $.

items.informal_name: bind₁ Applied to a Monomial Yields Product of Substitutions
items.type:
∀ {σ : Type u_1} {τ : Type u_2} {R : Type u_3} [inst : CommSemiring R] (f : σ → MvPolynomial τ R) (d : σ →₀ ℕ) (r : R),
  (MvPolynomial.bind₁ f) ((MvPolynomial.monomial d) r) = MvPolynomial.C r * ∏ i ∈ d.support, f i ^ d i
items.informal_description: For any substitution function $ f : \sigma \to R[\tau] $, finite exponent vector $ d : \sigma \to_0 \mathbb{N} $, and coefficient $ r \in R $, applying the variable substitution homomorphism $ \text{bind}_1 $ to the monomial $ \text{monomial}(d, r) $ results in the product of the constant polynomial $ C(r) $ and the product over $ f(i)^{d(i)} $ for all $ i $ in the support of $ d $. Formally, $ \text{bind}_1(f)(\text{monomial}(d, r)) = C(r) \cdot \prod_{i \in \text{support}(d)} f(i)^{d(i)} $.

items.informal_name: Multiplication by a Variable Preserves Coefficient Submodule Membership
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_2} {S : Type u_3} {σ : Type u_4} [inst : CommSemiring R] [inst_1 : CommSemiring S] [inst_2 : Module R S]
  {M : Submodule R S} {p : MvPolynomial σ S} {s : σ},
  p * MvPolynomial.X s ∈ MvPolynomial.coeffsIn σ M ↔ p ∈ MvPolynomial.coeffsIn σ M
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ in the multivariate polynomial ring $ R[\sigma] $, multiplying $ p $ by the variable $ X_s $ results in a polynomial with coefficients in the submodule $ M $ if and only if $ p $ itself has coefficients in $ M $. Formally, $ p \cdot X_s \in \text{coeffsIn}(\sigma, M) $ if and only if $ p \in \text{coeffsIn}(\sigma, M) $.
